A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same paper, including Appendices A–D. Their text, equations, algorithms, figures and tables can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama/Mistral experiments in Section 4, synthetic simulations in Appendix C, and TruthfulQA and GPT-OSS evaluations in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and simulations, including the model results in Table 2 and the additional comparisons in Tables 10–13.

M1.justification: The exact one-sided McNemar test, three aggregation methods, dataset-trimming procedure and Appendix D permutation extensions are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Leaderboard v2 tasks, MMLU-Pro trimming scenario, TruthfulQA evaluation, GPT-OSS GPQA/AIME25 evaluations and synthetic scenarios.

E2.justification: The same accuracy-drop and flip-probability heuristics are evaluated in Section 4. Appendix D retains the same binary, permutation, threshold and win-rate comparisons; the added citations introduce no evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Sample selections, model configurations, scoring metrics and testing procedures are unchanged. This includes the 70B MATH exclusion, hardware comparisons and GPT-OSS context-length conditions.

E4.justification: The dataset-reduction analysis, synthetic error-control and power experiments, and binary-versus-continuous-score analyses are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same standard errors, p-values and uncertainty procedures. The 1,000 synthetic experiments per configuration, ten MMLU-Pro runs and 24 evaluations per GPT-OSS example are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains the 70B KV-FP8 degradation of 0.29% and pooled p-value of 2.51e-02.

T1.justification: The definitions, Fact 1, power derivation, Appendix B variance derivation and Appendix D mathematical arguments are unchanged. Moving Fact 1 to the next page and restoring a comma in the joint-variable notation are presentation edits.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and concluding discussion retain the same contributions and scope, including controlled degradation testing, three aggregation approaches and detection of approximately 0.3% accuracy degradations.

C2.justification: The interpretations, applicability boundaries and limitations remain unchanged. Replacing 'detect the accuracy' with 'detect the degradation' on page 9 clarifies the existing statement without changing its meaning.

D1.justification: Software versions, hardware, checkpoint identifiers, inference flags, permutation settings and code-access information are unchanged in Section 4 and the appendices.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds Heineman et al. (2025) on dataset properties that distinguish models and cites Miller (2024) for uncertainty overestimation when paired evaluations are treated as independent. Miller is also added to Figure 1's caption, with both works added to the bibliography.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammatical, punctuation and notation corrections across the main text and Appendix D, alongside the short related-work addition. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption gains a citation, and the captions of Tables 2 and 5 correct 'Llama-3.1B' to 'Llama-3.1'. There is modest text and table reflow, including Fact 1 moving between pages, without new or redesigned displays.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves scholarly attribution through the Heineman and Miller references and improves clarity through wording and caption corrections. These are limited gains; the methods, empirical evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
